goal:
Introduce the key terms of our agentic AI module, sized by importance and grouped by theme:
- Building blocks: AI agent (10), LLM (9), RAG (8), tool calling (7), prompt (7), MCP server (6), context window (5), embeddings (5), vector store (4)
- Safety and trust: guardrails (8), human in the loop (8), hallucination (7), evaluation (6), PII masking (4), audit trail (3)
- Delivery: orchestration (6), multi-agent (5), token cost (4), latency (3), fine-tuning (3)

spec.title: Key terms of agentic AI
spec.objective: Learners see which terms matter most in this module and which theme each belongs to, before the lesson starts.

recommended.why: A word cloud gives an at-a-glance hook for the module vocabulary, with size for importance and colour for theme.

alternative.why: Visual impact versus accurate comparison: can learners tell which term matters most?

assumptions: Importance scores (1-10) are illustrative judgements for this module, not measured frequencies
Three themes: building blocks, safety and trust, delivery
Terms with equal importance are ordered alphabetically
spec.checkDescription: Every term appears once, in importance order, the count matches the slider, and only the chosen theme is highlighted.

learnerPrompts.predict: Before you look closely: which theme do you think has the most terms in the top 8?
learnerPrompts.explain: Compare the versions. In which one could you say exactly where “Guardrails” ranks, and why?

versions.explanation: D3 with the d3-cloud layout places each term once, sized by importance and coloured by theme, all horizontal so they read easily. The layout uses a seeded random source, so it stays stable when you change the sliders; playback only reveals the words in rank order. It is a strong hook, but word length distorts importance: long terms look bigger than their score.
caveats: Terms that do not fit at the current size are dropped and reported on screen.

versions.explanation: Chart.js shows the same terms as a ranked horizontal bar chart, largest at the top, coloured by theme. Playback reveals the bars in the same order as the cloud. It is less eye-catching, but learners can read each term's exact rank and compare any two terms.

three.js places the same terms on a slowly turning helix, most important at the top, with words at the back faded. Drag to orbit. It looks striking, but depth adds no information here: terms hide behind each other and rank is harder to read than in either 2D version.
caveats: Needs WebGL; on machines without a graphics card it can be slow or blank.
